BACKGROUND The University of Rhode Island is seeking a dedicated and qualified vendor to provide emergency and routine utility maintenance and repair services for all underground and above -ground utility systems , excluding electrical , located on the Kingston, Narragansett Bay and W.
Alton Jones campuses .
These critical systems include steam, water (potable and non-potable), sewage, storm water, natural gas, propane and heating oil.
The Kingston campus consists of 197 buildings totaling over 4 million square feet with miles of underground utility systems.
URI owned utility systems on the Kingston campus include a central steam plant, steam and condensate distribution/return network s, Five natural gas distribution networks, sewer collection system with four sewer pump stations, potable water supply and distribution, oil and propane fuel storage tanks for heating systems and a stormwater collection system.
The 153 acre Narragansett Bay Campus consists of 41 buildings and 326,000 square feet.

Utilities include natural gas supplied by RIE and distributed by URI owned piping network, potable water provided by the town and distributed by URI owned piping network, sewer collected by URI owned piping network and sent to the town for treatment, stormwater collection sy stem and oil and propane fuel storage for heating and generators.
The W.
Alton Jones campus is a rural campus in West Greenwich, RI and composed of 30 buildings.
Utilities include three small public water systems, septic systems, propane and oil storage for heating systems.
The selected vendor must have a thorough understanding of connection and repair methods for each of these utilities and an integral understanding of each of the university’s utility systems is necessary for undertaking the scope of work described in Section B of this solicitation.
The vendor shall demonstrate troubleshooting of utility outages and methods of providing control of the utility network and temporary service.
As such, the selected vendor(s) will be required to study and understand the universi ty’s utility systems within the first 6 months of the contract’s award date.

The selected vendor(s) will be required to provide routine and emergency service for pipefitter, steamfitter and plumbing services, along with all construction equipment, excavation services and materials required to perform the necessary task/repair.
Services shall also include investigation as necessary to ensure proper repair (locating, camera work, transit level, etc).
For clarification, the University will continue to utilize the State Master Price Agreement for general plumbing (MPA #40) and steamfitter work (MPA #199) for repairs and maintenance outside of the scope of utilities.

Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: June 15, 2026 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of a Contract in Excess of $5 Million: Chiller Maintenance and Repair Purpose of Submittal: The purpose of this action item is to seek Board of Trustees approval, under the Policy on Approval and Execution of Contracts and Other Binding Documents, of a new contract for the Facilities Operations group.
This contract represents ongoing support services which are part of the current operations of the campus for service and repair to the University’s chillers and HVAC systems.
The contract for these services has not yet been awarded, but is expected to be awarded by the State to begin July 1, 2026.
This proposed contract will replace the award previously approved by the Board in November 2023 for $6M over three years.
Because this proposed contract is in the bid award determination process , no supplier is identified at this time.

Once the State is ready to award the contract to the successful bidder, we anticipate that contract value to be closer to $5.0M, but we are requesting approval for a cap of $5.50M on the contract to allow for flexibility.
The targeted $5.0M expense is less than the prior contract for similar services because certain components of the contract have been updated and certain services split out to better serve the University.
Recommendation: It is recommended that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the proposed award for the Chiller Maintenance and Repair contract, which is expected to be issued for July 1, 2026.
Points to Consider: This prior contract approved by the Board of Trustees in November of 2023 exceeded its original estimated value largely due to unanticipated emergency repairs and required equipment replacement.
To better assess the new contract, the Facilities Operations group completed a comprehensive review of the services provided and decided to split out certain components of the work to better foster competition.

To meet the HVAC and chiller maintenance and repair needs of the University th rough this new time and materials contract, the University is proposing a $5.50M cap to the spend that includes unanticipated emergencies.
The University’s Facilities Operations group continues to work with URI Purchasing to maximize contracting options for HVAC equipment replacement, as well as preventative maintenance and repair.
